processing: An appellation rather than one recipe: green teas of several shapes, including Ziyang Maojian, Ziyang Cuifeng and Ziyang Yinzhen, each with its own process.
harvest_season: Spring is the main season, as is usual for Chinese named green teas; the exact picking depends on the product within the appellation.
appearance_dry: Varies by product, from round downy strands to fine needles, generally bright green.
appearance_liquor: Typically a clear pale green, as in Ziyang Maojian, its best-described member.
appearance_wet: Varies by product; the better grades show tender, whole, bright green buds and leaves.
taste_profile: Depends on the product; Ziyang Maojian, the usual reference, is fresh and mellow with a sweet finish. Selenium itself is not something you taste.

brewing.notes: General guidance for Chinese spring greens; adjust to the shape of the tea, and use slightly cooler water for fine needles.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year green tea, usually under the spring harvest, with the specific product and grade named on the pack. Like other greens it is for drinking fresh rather than ageing. The protected mark applies only to producers approved within the defined townships.
description:
Ziyang Selenium Tea is a protected name rather than a single tea. It covers green teas from Ziyang county in southern Shaanxi, on the upper Han River below the Daba Mountains, where the soils are naturally rich in selenium.

Within the name you will find different products, among them Ziyang Maojian, Ziyang Cuifeng and Ziyang Yinzhen. So the label tells you where the tea grew, while the product name tells you how it was made and what shape to expect.

Flavour follows the product. A good Maojian gives a fresh, mellow cup with a sweet finish, and brewing is the same as for other Chinese spring greens: use cooler water, not boiling.

Much of the marketing makes large promises about anti-ageing and cancer prevention. Those are promotional claims and no reason to buy a tea. Buy it as you would any spring green, for freshness and a clean aroma, and look for the specific product name rather than the word selenium alone.
history:
Ziyang is an old tea district, but this name is modern. Selenium in Ziyang tea came to attention through work by the Shaanxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences in the late 1970s and early 1980s, and the county has built its identity on it since.

Protection followed in stages. The area was defined in 2004 as twenty townships and towns of the county. The geographical-indication trademark was recognised as a well-known Chinese mark in 2012, and in 2020 the name joined the second list under the China-EU geographical indications arrangement.
